prerequisites: A competence in English corresponding at least to B1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFRL)

learning_outcomes.text: Reach a language competence in English corresponding to level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR), in relation to the four basic language skills (listening, speaking, reading, writing), with special emphasis on some genres of specialised and professional communication, such as project descriptions, project proposals for design competitions and reports.
Understand globally and selectively both oral and written texts on topics belonging to the personal and social sphere and to English for IT Engineering.

Take part in conversations and interact in discussions in a way appropriate to the context in different social and professional communicative situations; being able to write simple texts of personal and professional content.

Produce linear and cohesive oral and written texts to refer facts and describe situations connected to personal experiences and to the specialised field of IT Engineering; analysing, rephrasing and summarising simple texts on professional topics.

Mesoamerican civilization is a broad term that covers many different cultures, including the Olmec, Maya, Zapotec, Teotihuacan, Toltec, Mixtec, and Aztec civilizations. These societies were located in what is now Central and South America. They are known for their impressive architectural achievements, including pyramids, temples, and cities. They also developed sophisticated systems of writing, mathematics, and astronomy. Many of these civilizations also had complex social structures and religious beliefs. Despite their many similarities, each Mesoamerican civilization had its own unique characteristics and cultural practices. For example, the Maya were known for their advanced understanding of astronomy and their intricate calendar system, while the Aztecs were known for their military prowess and their human sacrifices.

Reflect on the linguistic system (phonology, morphology, syntax, lexicon) and on language uses (functions, variety of registers and texts, etc.), also in a comparative perspective, in order to identify analogies and differences with the Italian language.

Acquire skills and competences useful to obtain success in the world of work and in society (life skills e soft skills); reinforcing foreign language learning strategies in order to develop study autonomy; enhancing professional lexis and topics in the English language, by using texts and materials drawn from various sources.

syllabus_topics: English for Special Purposes (ESP), namely technical language for IT Engineering
Grammar and syntax of B2 CEFRL levels: nouns and articles
Expressing habits: "be used to", "used to", "get used to"
Formal and written English vs spoken English
Communicative functions of B2 CEFR Levels: talking about oneself and other people
Describing actions (habits and ongoing actions), places, people and professions
Writing an email and an accurate CV
Taking part effectively in job interviews
Topics and specific lexis: Italian, British and American education systems
A university in an English speaking country
Phonetic transcription and pronunciation in keeping with the International Phonetic Alphabet
Main varieties of English: British and American Englishes
Specific lexicon related to IT Engineering within the topics dealt with during the course

teaching_methods: Active participation of students through guided tasks and oral presentations
assessment_rules: The final exam consists of a written test and an oral interview, each making up 50% of the final mark. To pass the written test, a mark of at least 18/30 is required. Passing the written test is a precondition for accessing the oral test. The oral test assesses grammar accuracy, linguistic variety, pronunciation and intonation, ability to interact, language fluency, and appropriateness of micro-language.
